headline: Shaun Partners' Adam Dulles rates Nickel Industries a sell given depressed nickel price outlook and better commodity alternatives.
reasoning: The nickel price has been depressed and could remain so for another one to two years. Nickel Industries is transitioning from Nickel Pig Iron to a more diversified Indonesian nickel producer, including a Nickel Cobalt project, but this transition takes time. Major miners like BHP have exited nickel, signalling sector weakness. Adam sees far better commodity opportunities elsewhere.
quote: This is a tough one. I guess the share price doesn't really show it, but the share price for Nickel Industries is very, very difficult as far as that. It is a business and the nickel price has been certainly in the doghouse, if I could say that, and potentially will continue to be in the doghouse for another year or two years as well. So they are changing the business, transitioning the business from a Nickel Pig Iron producer to more of a diversified Indonesian Nickel producer. But in time that does, yeah, that's probably a better chart to look at. It really hasn't done much. And BHP has got out of Nickel. We've seen other big companies starting to move... overall, this one is not for me and we've got way better commodities to go out there. So it's a sell from me.

headline: Nickel Industries declined in July due to Indonesian regulatory volatility and sulphuric acid supply disruptions stemming from Middle East tensions.

headline: Henry Jennings holds Nickel Industries with tentative upside to 95c-$1, but sees it as hostage to Indonesian government and nickel price
reasoning: Henry notes NIC has fallen from $1.10 to 88 cents and broker target prices suggest upside. A recent framework agreement with Indonesian partners on high pressure acid leach processing is somewhat positive. The stock is trying to form a base around 85-87 cents and could recover to 95c-$1 if commodities run. However, it remains highly exposed to Indonesian government policy risk, which Henry considers harder to predict than the nickel price itself.
quote: It's an interesting one, isn't it? It's very much beholden to the Indonesian government and their whim in terms of what they're going to do with Nickel exports, etc. They have just done a deal recently with a framework agreement with its Indonesian partners. So they're looking at strategic cooperation in the high pressure acid leach processing... Probably the Indonesian government moves are probably harder to predict than the Nickel price. So I have a tentative hold.

headline: Luke Laird top pick Nickel Industries for 30-40% upside on 30% free cash flow yield into FY27 and vertically integrated low-cost model
reasoning: Nickel Industries' vertical integration in Indonesia means it benefits from rising nickel prices without the same margin compression that hits sulfide producers. Laird estimates a 30% free cash flow yield on the stock into FY27 with 30-40% price upside. The market is paying little attention to nickel names at present, creating a mispricing opportunity.
quote: We're actually estimating a 30 percent free cash flow yield on this stock into FY 27. So we don't think the market's sort of paying any attention to nickel mines at the moment... and see, you know, probably 30, 40 percent upside there.

headline: Firetail is a shareholder in Nickel Industries and sees the nickel price floor as established, with Indonesia's production discipline supporting a recovery.
reasoning: Indonesia's influence over nickel supply — through production caps and the economics of HPAL — means the market floor has been set and prices are recovering. Indonesia controls enough of the market to influence price and the carbon-intensive, high-cost nature of Indonesian laterite production means companies there need economic returns, supporting a price floor. Fist is not invested in nickel mines but holds Nickel Industries.
quote: I think it's pretty clear now that we've seen the floor price for nickel and we're on the way back up.
episode_title: Australia's Power Grid Is About to Break (Matt Fist)
